THE HEADLINES:

 

  1. Government announces subsidy of 62 thousand 370 crore rupees on phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for rabi season.
  2. Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units under PM Mudra Yojana and Stand-Up India Scheme till March 2031; Also clears extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector- 4.
  3. President Droupadi Murmu confers Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26; Ahmedabad and Sanand bag 1st prize in Swachh Shehar Jodi category; Navi Mumbai gets Swachh Sheher League award.
  4. Moody’s raises India’s GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent for current fiscal. 
  5. Russia and Ukraine reach agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange in US brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi.
  6. Niraj Kumar wins bronze in men’s 50 metre rifle three-positions event at World Shooting Championships in Doha; Also secures 2028 Los Angeles Olympics quota.

Government has approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for RABI Season, 2026-27 on Phosphatic and Potassic fertilizers. The tentative budgetary requirement for Rabi 2026-27 will be approximately 62 thousand 370 crore rupees. This is nearly 24 thousand 417 crore more than the budgetary requirement for Rabi 2025-26 season. Briefing media in New Delhi today after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the subsidy will ensure smooth availability of these fertilizers to the farmers at affordable prices. Mr. Vaishnaw said, the Cabinet has approved the continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. He said that the outlay of five thousand crore rupees is approved for guarantee and it is expected to support mudra loans worth 12.60 lakh crore rupees.

 

The Cabinet has also given nod to the continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and aims to provide financial assistance to additional 2.5 lakh entrepreneurs in a span of five years.

 

The Cabinet has also cleared the extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04 of Noida Metro Rail Project covering approximately 8.5 kilometres and comprising five elevated stations.

 

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi. Mr. Vaishnaw said, the Museum is envisaged as a landmark civilizational museum showcasing the continuity, diversity and richness of Bharat’s civilizational heritage through an integrated narrative of its tangible and intangible cultural heritage.

The Ministry of Defence has signed a contract worth over 498 crore rupees with Cochin Shipyard Limited for the Normal Refit and Re-powering of Indian Naval Ship, Betwa. The contract was inked in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi today.

 

The Defence Ministry said that under the contract, INS Betwa, a Brahmaputra-class frigate of the Indian Navy, will undergo a major propulsion system transformation.

           

The Ministry said that the project will provide a major impetus to the Government’s vision of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ and ‘Make-in-India’, while reinforcing the country’s indigenous naval ship repair and maintenance capabilities.

President Droupadi Murmu has said that the goal of cleanliness cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single institution alone and the participation of every citizen, every household, every community and every city is essential. Speaking after presenting Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 in New Delhi this evening, the President said, cleanliness is not merely a matter of maintaining the appearance of public spaces but it reflects health of citizens, social sensitivity and administrative accountability.

 

In his address, Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal said, with the beginning of Swachh Bharat Mission in 2014, cleanliness has become a mass celebration.

 

More from our correspondent:

 

“Swachh Survekshan has grown in scale from 73 ULBs in 2016 to over four thousand 751 cities in its latest edition. In Swachh Shehar Jodi category the 1st prize was presented to Ahmedabad and Sanand in Gujarat, the 2nd prize was given to Indore and Depalpur in Madhya Pradesh. 3rd Prize was presented to Tirupati and Kuppam in Andhra Pradesh. Swachh Sheher League award was given to Navi Mumbai, Surat and Vijaywada. GVMC Vishakhapatnam, Jabalpur and Lucknow were awarded as top three cities for cleanliness in more than 10 lakh population category. Rewa in Madhya Pradesh, Bilaspur in Chhatisgarh and Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh were presented awards as Swachh river front towns. Puri in Odisha got the 1st prize as Swachh Coastal Town and Rudrapur in Uttarakhand got 1st prize as Clean Himalayan city. The awards serve as a celebration of the collective achievements of cities and States in the past decade and a renewed commitment to sustain on-ground achievements. With Anand Kumar, Anupam Mishra, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

Northern Railway has made elaborate arrangements at major stations of Delhi Area for the convenience of passengers, especially those travelling to the Eastern parts of the country to celebrate the festival of Chhath. The Northern Railway is operating 31 Special trains from major railway stations in the Delhi region today. The move is aimed at facilitating passengers travelling to their native places to celebrate the festival. Tomorrow, the Railways will operate 29 special trains from the Delhi region.

External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari today launched the Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas website in New Delhi. The 19th Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas Convention will be held from 7 to 9th January next year in Kolkata. The theme: is “Return to Roots: Reigniting the Diaspora Connect with Bharat”. The Convention will be organized by the Ministry of External Affairs in partnership with the State Government of West Bengal.

India has offered to share its healthcare expertise, technical capabilities and best practices with fellow BIMSTEC member countries, emphasizing its commitment to strengthening regional cooperation in the health sector. Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda made the offer while addressing the inaugural BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting in Colombo, the first such gathering of health ministers and senior representatives from India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal and Thailand.

Moody’s Ratings has raised India’s GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent for the current fiscal year from its earlier projections of 6.5 per cent, citing strong domestic consumption, improving investment and the economy’s resilience to higher global energy prices.

 

In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28 report, the ratings agency said India’s economic growth is expected to remain near seven per cent over the medium term, with sustained private investment potentially pushing growth even higher. Moody’s also pointed to stronger capital goods production and imports, faster industrial credit growth and improving capacity utilisation as signs of a recovery in private investment.

 

It noted that the country has handled the global energy price shock better than previously expected, helped by its ability to diversify crude oil and gas supplies.

Russia and Ukraine have agreed in principle to a major prisoner-of-war exchange following two days of US-mediated negotiations in Abu Dhabi, although no breakthrough was reached on ending the nearly five-year conflict.

 

US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner described the trilateral talks as difficult but productive. Kushner said the agreement could lead to the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners since the war began, with final numbers expected to be confirmed shortly. Vladimir Medinsky, head of the Russian delegation at talks, told a press conference that details of the exchange would be announced soon and that negotiations would continue.

 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed the progress but insisted that European countries must be involved in negotiations concerning the continent’s security.

 

Washington has indicated support for European participation, particularly on security guarantees, while Moscow has questioned the need for European representatives in direct negotiations, arguing that their support for Ukraine makes them unsuitable as neutral participants.

The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning over Keralam, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry  and Karaikal for tomorrow. Similar conditions are expected over Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Muzaffarabad for the next two days.

Niraj Kumar today won the bronze medal in the men’s 50 metre rifle three-positions event at the World Shooting Championships in Doha. Niraj has also secured a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

 

This marks India’s second Olympic quota from the championships. Previously, Jaypal Malviya had secured the first quota by winning a silver medal in the men’s 10m air pistol event.

In Football, India today defeated Maldives 1-nil in SAFF Championship Group B match at the National Stadium in Dhaka. Suhail Ahmad Bhat scored the match’s lone goal from the penalty spot in the 38th minute. With this the Blue Tigers entered the semi-finals.

India today reiterated that its stance on the Russia-Ukraine conflict has been that peace can only be restored through diplomacy and dialogue. Briefing media this evening in New Delhi, Spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said, in recent months, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasized that endless war must give way to end of war.

 

       

On Strait of Hormuz, India continued to call for free and safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

 

       

On midterm elections in the US, the MEA Spokesperson said, the mid-term elections are an internal matter of the US. He emphasized that the India-United States relationship enjoys strong bipartisan support in the US and India continue to work to further strengthen its Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership with the US.

       

On the comments of U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom USCIRF, Mr Jaiswal said, the USCIRF is a biased and ill-informed organisation with a blatantly political agenda. He said, the USCIRF and its Commissioners have consistently chosen to remain silent on attacks on religious places in the US and on the hate crimes and racial abuse targeted at the Indian community in the US.

       

New Delhi condemned Chinese vloggers and livestreamers who were filming impoverished neighbourhoods of Dhaka in Bangladesh and falsely presenting the locations as parts of New Delhi, saying such efforts to portray a distorted picture of any country are unfortunate. 

On Capt Pant an Indian sailor currently in UK custody, Mr Jaiswal said, New Delhi continues to be in touch with the lawyers of Captain Ajit Pant, as also his family.

The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to apprise it about their proposed measures to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in the country. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked WhatsApp and similar intermediaries to simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C (Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre). The order regarding it uploaded on the website with regard to the hearing conducted on 29th of last month in a suo motu case titled ‘Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’,

       

The bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, has listed the plea for further consideration on 23rd of this month.

The Election Commission has said that restrictions and prohibitions applicable to serving government employees under the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) will also apply to retired government officials and other individuals engaged in various capacities by State and Union Territory governments.

       

The Commission has written a letter to the Chief Secretaries and Chief Electoral Officers of Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand in this regard where Assembly elections wil be held next year. We have a report –

 

       

 

 

“The Election Commission has said that such individuals must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns or canvassing. It also said that such individuals shall not summon any election related officer of the constituency or district where elections have been announced, for any official discussions or meetings or hold video conferences with any such officer. The Poll Body added that the provisions of the MCC apply to all organizations, corporations and commissions funded wholly or partially by the Government and their employees. It said, the relevant Conduct Rules, in the States, prohibit the Government servants from taking part in political activities and elections. With Anand Kumar, Anupam Mishra, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

President Droupadi Murmu has urged IPS officers to prioritise alleviating the fears of socially or economically weaker individuals who generally lack access to senior officials, and addressing their grievances. Addressing probationers of the 2025 batch of Indian Police Service today at Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President said for the citizens, police officers and constables are symbols of governance. She said, people perceive the governance to be good when the police system functions well. The President said that the People feel immensely supported when a police officer listens to their grievances with sensitivity and attentiveness.

 

       

President Murmu today also interacted with members of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups of disha at Rashtrapati Bhavan. On the occasion, she highlighted the transformative power of education and encouraged them to actively contribute to India’s developmental journey.

India’s water management initiatives have emerged as a model for developing countries. World Bank Global Director for Water, Saroj Kumar Jha, has described India’s progress as a remarkable success story. Speaking ahead of the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, Mr Jha praised initiatives such as the Jal Jeevan Mission, Namami Gange and Swachh Bharat Mission. He said the Jal Jeevan Mission had provided improved drinking water access to 800 million people in less than seven years. He also lauded efforts to clean the Ganga and strengthen the safety of nearly 900 dams.

In view of the Chhath festival, Northern Railway has planned to run 31 special trains from major stations in the Delhi area from tomorrow. Northern Railway has made elaborate arrangements at major railway stations in the Delhi area to manage the rush of passengers travelling to their native places to celebrate the Chhath festival, particularly those heading towards eastern parts of the country.

       

 

 

Today, 27 special trains are being operated from major stations in the Delhi region. These include nine trains from Anand Vihar Terminal, six from New Delhi, five from Shakur Basti, three each from Delhi Junction and Hazrat Nizamuddin, and one from Rohtak.

In Uttarakhand, the portals of Shri Kedarnath and Yamunotri Dham will be closed for the winter season tomorrow on the occasion of Bhai Dooj. With this, the annual summer pilgrimage to both shrines will come to an end. Over 64 lakh devotees have visited the Char Dham shrines this year, marking a record turnout. Preparations for the closure of the temples are underway, and both shrines have been decorated with several quintals of flowers. We have more from our correspondent;

       

 

“The portals of Shri Kedarnath Dham, located in Rudraprayag district, will be closed for the winter season tomorrow at 8:30 AM, in accordance with Vedic rituals and religious traditions. Today, the ceremonial palanquin of Baba Kedar entered the temple premises. Following the closure, the ceremonial palanquin will proceed to the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath, the winter seat of Lord Kedarnath. Meanwhile, the portals of Shri Yamunotri Dham in Uttarkashi district will be closed tomorrow at 10:28 AM. Thereafter, the ceremonial palanquin of Goddess Yamuna will proceed to Kharsali, her winter abode. Devotees will be able to offer prayers and seek blessings of Goddess Yamuna at Kharsali during the next six months. Earlier today, the portals of Shri Gangotri Dham were also closed for the winter season on the occasion of the Annakoot festival. The ceremonial palanquin of Goddess Ganga will reach Mukhba village, her winter abode, tomorrow. Sakshi Singh, Akashvani News, Dehradun.”

Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has described his recent visit to Saudi Arabia as productive and meaningful, saying it further strengthened the bonds of friendship and cooperation between the two countries. During his visit, Mr Rijiju and Saudi Arabia’s Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Tawfiq bin Fawzan Al-Rabiah, signed the Bilateral Haj Agreement for 2027. Under the agreement, India has secured a quota of one lakh 75 thousand and 25 pilgrims. The two ministers also reviewed preparations for Haj 2027 and discussed key operational priorities to ensure a safe, smooth and well-organised pilgrimage for Indian pilgrims. In a social media post, Mr Rijiju said, India and Saudi Arabia share a strong commitment to the welfare of pilgrims and the successful conduct of Haj 2027.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. The Met Department has also forecast  thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow. The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India is now home to a hundred chess Grandmasters. Congratulating Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Chess Grandmaster, the Prime Minister said that India’s reaching 100 Grandmasters is a remarkable milestone that reflects the immense talent, dedication and hard work of Indian players as well as the growing popularity of chess among the youth. In a social media post, he also expressed delight that young chess talents emerging from different parts of the country are making their mark on the global stage. Mr Modi expressed hope that the achievement will inspire many more youngsters to take up chess and pursue excellence.

In the Under-19 Asia Cup Cricket, India secured a place in the semi-finals after defeating the United Arab Emirates by 70 runs at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman today.       Put into bat first, India set a target of 310 runs and then restricted the UAE to 239 runs in 50 overs. India had scored 309 losing 7 wickets in 50 overs. India’s Aryavir Sehwag was named Player of the Match for his impressive knock of 160 off 168 balls. India will now take on Afghanistan in the semi-final on Thursday.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today spoke to President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy who shared his perspective on recent developments related to the ongoing conflict. During the telephonic conversation, the Prime Minister reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. Mr Modi conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict.

         

 

The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors for the mutual benefit of the people of both countries.

Russia battered Ukraine’s power grid again and Ukrainian forces hit another of Russia’s biggest oil refineries hours before delegations from Moscow and Kyiv were due to meet for new US-brokered talks to end the ongoing crisis. Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators are set to hold two-day talks in Abu Dhabi from tomorrow, marking their first meeting since February.

 

 

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov today said that US President Donald Trump’s team has placed collective security covering not just Russia and Ukraine but also a wider area, at the top of the agenda for the two days of discussions.

 

 

Security guarantees are expected to dominate the discussions, amid continuing hostilities and intensified missile and drone attacks by both sides.

 

 

Meanwhile, European participation remains contentious, with Moscow opposing their involvement at this stage.

India and European Union today reviewed the full spectrum of bilateral partnership and progress in implementing the Joint Comprehensive Strategic Agenda. The 7th India- EU strategic partnership review meeting was held in New Delhi. It was co-chaired by the Secretary (West) in the External Affairs Ministry Sibi George and Deputy Secretary-General for Geoeconomics and Interinstitutional Issues of the European Union Matti Maasikas. Both sides welcomed the very positive momentum in the India-EU relations. External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that both sides reviewed engagements towards boosting trade and investment cooperation, including the timely signing and implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement. Our correspondent reports that the discussions also covered strengthening supply chains and economic security.

 

 

        

         

 

“India and EU discussed cooperation on critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, digital public infrastructure, advanced semiconductors, clean tech and biotechnology. They expressed satisfaction on deepening research collaboration, including India’s potential association with Horizon Europe. The two sides underscored the importance of strengthening connectivity partnership including Global Gateway, India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor and trilateral projects in clean energy, climate resilience, green mobility and digitalisation. Suparna Saikia, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri reached Paris today for the third India-France Strategic Dialogue on Space and the first Dialogue on Economic Security and Critical Technologies. Indian Embassy in France said in a social media post that these discussions will deepen cooperation between both nations in the fields of space, critical technologies and economic security.

Twenty four fishermen hailing from Thoothukudi were released from the Maldives prison yesterday. They were arrested by the Maldives Navy for trespassing into international waters while fishing in the Arabian Sea on last month. Fishermen were sent by a flight to Thiruvananthapuram. The officials of Tamil Nādu Fisheries Department received the fishermen at the airport and sent them to their native places.

The Delhi Government has notified the Delhi (Right of Citizens to Time-Bound and Easy Delivery of Services) Act, 2026. The Act aims to ensure that government departments deliver services within prescribed timelines and officials responsible for unnecessary delays are held accountable. It will replace the existing time-bound service delivery law of 2011 with a more modern and accountable system. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that the government is committed to making Delhi’s governance system citizen-centric, responsive and accountable, ensuring that every eligible citizen receives services on time and without difficulty. More from our correspondent

 

 

 

         

 

“The new system will ensure that citizens do not have to wait indefinitely for government services as the citizens will have a statutory right to receive government services within a prescribed timeframe. For unnecessary delays in delivery of services, the concerned officer can be fined 250 rupees per day, up to a maximum of five thousand rupees. There is also a provision for a fine for improperly rejecting applications under the new framework. Once an application is received, the designated officer will be responsible for either delivering the service within the prescribed timeline or communicating the reason for its rejection in writing. The Delhi government said that every application will be assigned a unique application number, allowing applicants to track its status online.  WITH ANAND KUMAR , SHIVANG MISRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal will launch the recreational river cruise service along the Yamuna in Delhi tomorrow. Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta will also be present on the occasion. Developed along the Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur stretch of the river, the initiative aims to promote river-based tourism and offer visitors a new recreational experience in the national capital. Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said that ahead of the launch, trial runs of the cruise vessel were successfully conducted last month in the presence of senior officials from Inland Waterways Authority of India and the Delhi Government.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah, during his visit to Gujarat today, inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for development projects worth over 1,400 crore in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency. These projects have been undertaken by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

 

 

         

 

Mr. Shah inaugurated the newly constructed flyover connecting ISKCON Crossroads to Sanand in Ahmedabad and a newly constructed Urban Health Centre in Gota.

 

 

         

 

Addressing a public gathering on the occasion, he said that the Ministry of Home Affairs has resolved to make the country drug-free before 31 December 2029. The Home Minister urged Gujarat to take the lead and achieve the target of making the state drug-free before 31 December 2028, a year ahead of the national deadline. He also announced that a toll-free helpline, 1033, along with a dedicated control room, will become operational from 1 December.

The Northern Railways said that apart from the permanent Holding area in New Delhi, a permanent holding area has been recently commissioned at Anand Vihar Terminal this year. These holding areas are provided with UTS ticket counters, toilets, Automatic Ticket Vending Machines, Catering stalls and May I Help You Booths.

  In Bangladesh, Kali Puja, also known as Shyama Puja, was celebrated with religious fervour, devotion and enthusiasm. Hindu devotees gathered at temples and makeshift mandaps to offer prayers to Goddess Kali and mark the triumph of good over evil.

The UGC notified the 2026 regulations in January this year, replacing the 2012 framework. The court had also restored the 2012 regulations on an interim basis.
